title: Vagyok, vagy — and where van goes

sections.title: The present forms
sections.content: Use vagyok with én and vagy with te. With ő, Hungarian drops the verb entirely for saying who or what someone is: Ő Anna, not Ő van Anna. Nouns and adjectives don't need a "to be" in the third person present.

van does exist — you'll meet it soon meaning "is/there is" for location, like Itt van a kávé ("The coffee is here"). It's just not used for saying what something IS. Fun fact: Hungarian isn't alone in dropping the verb here — Russian and Arabic do the same trick in the present tense. You're not skipping a step; you're joining a large club of languages that don't bother with "is" when a noun already does the job.
